# Pocket AI Gateway

Pocket AI Gateway is an open-source, local-first AI gateway packaged as one Go executable with an embedded Next.js dashboard and two protected SQLite databases.

## Current implementation

- The runtime provides secure owner setup/recovery, users and sessions, scoped rotating API keys, limits/accounting, provider and public model configuration, inference, request history, audit, diagnostics, portable configuration, and encrypted backup/restore.
- `GET /healthz` returns process liveness.
- `GET /readyz` returns minimal database readiness.
- `GET /_/` opens the embedded dashboard.
- `GET /_/status/` shows the local runtime readiness screen.
- Implemented auth endpoints cover setup, activation, login/logout, current/all owned sessions, session revocation, password change, and `PATCH /api/v1/me`.
- Implemented management endpoints cover `/api/v1/admin/users`, owner transfer, one-time activation/recovery codes, and owned `/api/v1/keys` lifecycle/rotation.
- Implemented usage endpoints cover `/api/v1/usage`, unresolved accounting, key effective limits, policy management, price versions, repricing, adjustments, and projection status.
- A new instance opens owner setup in the dashboard. The first successful claim creates the sole owner account.
- Native OpenAI Chat/Responses/Responses input-token counting/embeddings/moderations/non-streaming image generation/edit/variation/buffered speech/multipart audio transcription and translation/models, Anthropic Messages/count_tokens/models, and Gemini generation/count/embedding/models are implemented. OpenAI Moderations preserve the native upstream taxonomy and require a moderation-capable target. Image, speech, transcription, and audio translation operations use dedicated scopes and capable targets with bounded bodies. OpenAI Responses includes gateway-owned storage, background execution, polling, cancellation, input items, deletion, native compaction through the OpenAI preset, direct input-token counting through capable OpenAI targets, key-owned Conversation CRUD, and atomic synchronous, background, or buffered-stream conversation attachment. It also supports bounded native web search for non-streaming stateless, stored, and background Responses on an OpenAI-adapter target using the built-in `openai` preset, with separate capability/scope/call accounting and unknown provider search cost. Attached streams require `store:false`; successful terminal events replay after Conversation persistence, while `response.failed` and `error` replay without changing the Conversation. Shared generation, function tools, image input, structured output, usage, and supported streams translate across the three provider families when semantics can be preserved. Anthropic streaming requires an Anthropic-compatible target because its first event needs input usage.
- Public models support fixed, ordered fallback, weighted, lowest estimated cost, and observed latency routing. Administrators can preview selection and rejection reasons without sending inference.
- Provider presets cover OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, and local Ollama. GitHub catalog refresh is opt-in and imports metadata candidates only.

## Stable namespace plan

- OpenAI-compatible API: `/api/openai/v1/`
- Anthropic-compatible API: `/api/anthropic/v1/`
- Gemini-compatible API: `/api/gemini/v1beta/`
- Gateway management API: `/api/v1/`
- Authentication API: `/api/v1/auth/`
- Administrative API: `/api/v1/admin/`

The URL path selects the client protocol. Headers never switch a request between OpenAI, Anthropic, or Gemini response formats.

## Operator commands

- `pocket-ai-gateway serve`
- `pocket-ai-gateway snapshot --output <directory>`
- `pocket-ai-gateway restore --snapshot <directory>`
- `pocket-ai-gateway backup --output <file.pagbak>`
- `pocket-ai-gateway restore-backup --archive <file.pagbak>`
- `pocket-ai-gateway owner-reset --data-dir <directory>`
- `pocket-ai-gateway version`

The server listens on `127.0.0.1:8080` and stores data in `pocket_gateway_data` unless flags or environment variables override those process settings.
